chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Rabīʿ al-Aṣamm, from al-Ḥārith ibn al-Mughīrah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who has a wife in Iraq, then commits illicit sexual intercourse while he is in the Ḥijāz. He said: “He is to be given the hadd of the fornicator: one hundred lashes, and he is not to be stoned.”

I said: What if he is with her in one town, but he is confined in a prison and cannot go out to her, nor can she enter upon him—what do you think if he commits zina in the prison? He said: “He is in the position of one whose family is absent from him; he is to be lashed one hundred lashes.”

key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ الْغَائِبِ: legally treated like one absent from his spouse
key_terms.فُجُورًا: illicit sexual misconduct committed by the man in this report
key_terms.لَا يُرْجَمُ: he is not punished by stoning
key_terms.مَحْبُوسٌ فِي سِجْنٍ: confined in prison and unable to access his wife
key_terms.مِائَةَ جَلْدَةٍ: one hundred lashes as the hadd punishment in this case
key_terms.يُضْرَبُ حَدَّ الزَّانِي: the prescribed legal punishment for the fornicator is to be carried out

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for zina if a married man is away from his wife or unable to reach her?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on the hadd punishment for zina when a man has a wife but is effectively unable to access her. The Imam عليه السلام rules that physical separation or imprisonment places him in the legal position of one absent from his spouse, so the punishment is one hundred lashes rather than rajm.
